messages:
samira: Hey team — staging started returning 401 invalid_api_key for a service that was working this morning. We rolled a VSCode snippet pack for onboarding yesterday, and I suspect it touched a few stored secrets. Error from our client: {\"error\":\"invalid_api_key\",\"message\":\"API key not found\"}. Anyone seen snippet auto-rewrites cause this?

support-bot: Created internal ticket INC-5129 and attached request-id suggestions.

alex: Can you paste a sanitized curl example and the x-request-id from the failing request headers? Also confirm whether the Authorization header is sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `Api-Key:` etc.

samira: Sure — minimal repro we used (key redacted):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_KEY" \\ \  https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/complete -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
Response headers: `x-request-id: rq_ab12cd34`
Response body: `{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key not found"}`
I validated the key in our vault (looks correct), but when I pasted it into a local env var via the snippet it failed.

morgan: VSCode snippet packs can run formatters or autocomplete. Common culprits: smart punctuation (three dots -> ellipsis), invisible joiners, soft-hyphen, or trimming. Two quick checks: 1) compare raw byte output of the key with the dashboard copy using `printf '%s' \"$KEY\" | xxd -p` on mac/linux; 2) check length/charset with `echo -n \"$KEY\" | wc -c` and `echo -n \"$KEY\" | LC_ALL=C sed -n 'l'` to reveal escapes.

alex: Also check that the snippet extension doesn't add a trailing newline or wrap key in quotes. Example I saw before: `"sk_..."` (with quotes) or `…` (unicode ellipsis) replacing `...`. Those will cause a mismatch but often show up as valid-looking string.

samira: Ran the xxd diff between dashboard copy and the env var produced by the snippet. Dashboard key hex starts with `73 6b 5f 6c...` while the snippet copy shows a different sequence: `73 6b 5f 6c ... e2 80 a6 ...` — the `e2 80 a6` is the UTF-8 ellipsis. Turns out my onboarding snippet had `...` in the template and VSCode auto-converted it to `…`. That mutated the key. Replacing `…` with three ascii dots and re-uploading the key fixed staging immediately.

morgan: Good catch. For prevention: we should add a small client-side validation in our SDKs to reject keys containing non-ASCII or control bytes and return a more actionable error than generic invalid_api_key. Also update the onboarding snippet text to use a placeholder that won't trigger formatting (e.g., `<YOUR_KEY_HERE>`).

alex: For support playbook: search logs for keys failing length/utf-8 pattern and surface a support hint: "check for smart quotes/ellipsis and zero-width chars; copy from Dashboard". We can also detect non-ASCII in the auth parsing layer and return `invalid_api_key: malformed_characters` with a note to copy from dashboard.

samira: That workaround worked for us. Created a new dashboard key and pasted via raw copy button (no snippet). Staging is green again. Thanks all :thumbsup:

morgan: I'll file a docs/quickfix and a small SDK PR to validate charset. Assigning follow-up to eng-oncall to consider server-side hinting.

samira: Marking INC-5129 as resolved on our end — leaving ticket for product/docs follow-up.
